author: Kyla
title: Top 10 Best Disney Villain Songs - NewsBreak
text:
By Kyla ,
33 minutes ago
10. "Mine, Mine, Mine" The song "Mine, Mine, Mine" is the song of the villain from Pocahontas , Governor Ratcliffe. Ratcliffe, in my opinion, is not Disney's best villain, nor his most well-known, but he deserves to be acknowledged because his song represents something that is at the root of humanity: Greed.
Disney 9. "Mad Madam Mim" "Mad Madam Mim" is that very woman describing herself to a young King Arthur in a timeless classic, The Sword in the Stone . Madam Mim is actually one of my favorite villains; she is very humorous. Although I do love her, she didn't score higher because I think other villains and songs are higher than this absolutely gorgeous queen.
Disney Related: Eat A H ge Pile Of Food And I'll Reveal Which Season You're Most Like
8. "Who's Been Painting My Roses Red?" We all have to appreciate the underrated Queen of Hearts, and what better way than to acknowledge her song in the countdown? A phrase people will often recognize is that of this absolutely berserk woman, "Who's been painting my roses red?" Her villain song is super recognizable and very well done, but she doesn't get a higher spot because there are others who just did better.
Disney 7. "Queen of Mean" Alright... Hear me out on this one. "Queen of Mean" from Descendants 3 is one of the catchiest villain songs. Audrey fits the song perfectly, and it is performed well. Although not traditional Disney, this song deserves attention from the sheer underrated villain that sings it and the vibes it brings. It's giving vicious, and I'm TOTALLY here for it.
David Bukach / ©Disney Channel / courtesy Everett Collection Related: Your Pizza Choices Will Reveal The Exact Way You Express Love In Relationships
6. "Poor Unfortunate Souls" I would place this closer to 1, but I also want to include other songs. So, our queen Ursula from The Little Mermaid misses the top 5. She is an icon, and this song is absolutely flawless. It's great to sing along to, and it makes me feel evil when I hear it. Ursula is one of the best and most recognized Disney villains, and for good reasons. She slays the screen whenever she's on it, and she actually has a pretty flawless plan.
Disney 5. "Gaston" You guys had to have guessed this song would be in this list. LeFou and Gaston are both absolutely flawless in this funky, upbeat, catchy song about the legend himself, Gaston. Though I personally am not the biggest fan of Gaston, this song does deserve recognition for just being the funky song it is. This song isn't what defines Gaston's villainy, but it does display his pride, and LeFou does a bang-up job of stroking that massive ego.
Disney Related: Pick Your Favorite Random Characters And We'll Reveal Your Inner Disney Princess
4. "In the Dark of the Night" Rasputin is one of my favorite Disney villains. From the movie Anastasia , this barely-staying-together villain can sing a bop and be hugely hilarious. He is an icon. His song is a representation of his hatred for Anastasia and is literally just a bop that is based on haunting her dreams. But all in all, this song is thoroughly enjoyable, and I honestly love it.
Disney 3. "Mother Knows Best" This song is GORGEOUS. Mother Gothel is an absolutely evil person, but she knows how to belt out a song. This is the song from Tangled that is THE most popular, and it deserves to be. Gothel is an amazing villain with shallow reasoning, but her ability to manipulate Rapunzel is startling. This song is a well-written display of that, and I LOVE it.
Disney Related: Build A Dream Cast For A Fake Netflix Show And I’ll Tell You If It Gets Canceled Or Renewed
2. "Be Prepared" What else could get this close than this song? Scar is a legend, and this song is jaw-dropping. When watching the movie, the animation is brilliant, and even just listening to the song, my jaw drops. Scar hits all the notes, and the hyenas as his comedic sidekicks were the perfect choice. I love this song, and it would have been number 1 if I had a reason to make it better than #1.
Disney 1. "Hellfire" Frollo's song from the Hunchback of Notre Dame has EARNED this spot. From the animations ACING our screens with the imagery of Esmeralda IN the fire, and displaying Frollo's loss of control within religion, to the absolute perfection of the song and its meaning, there is no other song that possibly compares for me. I love this song and its context with my entire soul, and it should be more widely known than it is. If you don't want to listen to an old guy sing it, though, there is a JAWDROPPING cover by Annapantsu.
